title: Salt Water (main titles)
note: Two-note synth ostinato under a slow pad, fretless bass, gated snare entering on the cut to the boat. Ends hard on the stand-down order.

title: Bullpen hum
note: No melody. Fluorescent buzz, a wall of televisions, rain against the blinds, and one held low pad. The bullpen is the only room in the film with no tune in it.

title: Salsa on the watchman's radio
note: Tinny salsa from an empty container office, playing to nobody. It keeps running under the counting.

title: Nineteen (pulse)
note: A single low pulse, one hit per crate number. Stops dead when Lupe runs.

title: Six Weeks (Crockett)
note: The Burnett cue: a clean Prophet pad with a sax-like lead that never quite resolves. Every time it plays, Crockett is alone in the frame.

title: Cafecito radio
note: Latin pop and a call-in show, always from a small speaker in another room. Little Havana is never scored.

title: Ball game on the radio
note: A ball game at low volume in the bookie's back room. The only thing in the room that isn't afraid.

title: Nassau
note: Steel drum, fretless bass, a clean guitar with a lot of chorus. This is the money cue: it plays whenever the word Salt Water is said out loud.

title: Piano bar standard
note: A house pianist playing something with too many chords. Same tune in both Carlyle scenes.

title: Nineteen (fire)
note: No drums anywhere in this stretch. A low drone, rain hissing on hot metal, and one high held note at the number on the crate.

title: You Belong to the City
note: Licensed period song, used twice: once driving east into the light with a car telephone ringing, once on the causeway at dawn with the top down. Sax and a long tail under the dialogue.

title: Ocean Drive (cruise)
note: Mid-tempo synth with a brushed snare. The driving cue. Never used over a scene with a dead body in it.

title: Dog track PA and crowd
note: The announcer, the crowd, the dogs. Switek's whole world in one speaker.

title: Smuggler's Blues
note: Licensed period song. First over the parking lot where Switek takes two thousand dollars; reprised instrumentally over the crates sitting in the sun at the tag.

title: Rooftop (near silence)
note: Gravel, rain, a dog two canals away, water on a seawall. Almost no score at all - the one place the film refuses to help itself.

title: Badge number
note: Solo synth and the tape hiss of a recorder running. Reprised when the tape goes in the water.

title: Smooth Operator
note: Licensed period song, playing in the suite while Marta explains that the truth is a thing you schedule.

title: Two-lane (Everglades)
note: Engine, cicadas, the cooling unit cycling on and off, and a slow synth figure with no percussion. Long.

title: Airstrip
note: Prop wash, generator putt-putt, a shovel in dirt, and a low brass synth. The shovel is louder than the music.

title: Issued by us
note: One held chord, played once, allowed to decay into the teletype.

title: Cover band at the Miramar
note: A band playing something fast and wrong. Cuts dead on the loading bay and does not come back.

title: The jacket
note: Solo piano-register synth, no percussion. Burnett's theme, resolved and then put away.

title: Storm (raid build)
note: The main-title ostinato returns, faster, with rain on the roof and radios.

title: Racking
note: Percussive, gated snare, steel drum. The loudest cue in the film.

title: Prieto
note: Everything drops out except water on the roof. Four seconds of nothing, then the next scene starts loud.

title: In the Air Tonight
note: Licensed period song. The causeway standoff: the drum break lands on the moment Tubbs lowers the gun. A deliberate echo of the pilot, and the only time the film plays it.

title: Crockett's Theme
note: Licensed period cue under the two-man scene on Ocean Drive. Sax lead, no drums for the first minute.

title: Nineteen (coda)
note: The crate-number pulse returns on a solo synth, slower, under a child saying a number out loud at a grave.

title: Salt Water (end titles)
note: Main-title ostinato, resolved at last, with the sax lead from the Burnett cue. Two minutes, then a radio crackling into the next case.
